sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 18.09.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 18.09.2023. at about 2-00 p.m., the petitioner was walking on footpath road in order to cross the road near Sundahalli Village Sravanabelagola Hobli,
Channarayapattna Taluk Hassan District, at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 came from Shravanabelagola side, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital at Sravanabelagola, wherein first aid treatment was given, later shifted to Punya Hospital at Channarayapattna, wherein petitioner took treatment.

Thereafter he was referred to ESI hospital at Bengaluru wherein he also took treatment and later he was shifted to AIMS hospital at B.G.Nagar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery by spending Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 43 years and he was doing agricultural work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1-owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence he has been placed exparte.
After service of summons, the respondent No.2- insurer has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.

The respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the involvement of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 in the alleged accident.
It has contended that non-compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the rider of the motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence and FC at the time of accident.

Further contended that there is a undue delay of 2 days in the lodging of the Manje Gowda vs Harish .H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178535339/
2 complaint.

Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, the petitioner's age, occupation,
income and injuries suffered by him.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 by its rider, in RTA took place on 18.09.2023 at about 2.00 p.m. on Sundahali Village,
Sravanabelagola Hobli, Channarayapat- tna Taluk District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount & from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17.
Further examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P18 to Ex.P23.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its official as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, IMV notice and reply, charge sheet along with statements and vehicle release mahazar which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 10.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR was registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Prasana, who is the relative of the petitioner and an eyewitness to the accident by alleging the rash and negligent riding by the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.
In continuation the IO drawn spot mahazar and seizer mahazar as per Ex.P3 and Ex.P4.

On perusal of Ex.P3, the exact Manje Gowda vs Harish .H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178535339/
3 accident spot is on footpath.
) Thereby it is found that the rider of offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 by riding his motor cycle in rash and negligent manner dashed against petitioner in a foot path.
This once again evidentiates that the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA- 54-R-0471 was negligent as such he entered in to footpath and caused accident instead of proceeding in road.
10. The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the offending rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 has got damaged in MV front number plate, front mark scratched, front bungee scratched.
The IMV report marked at Ex.P.5 proves the involvement of the vehicle.
11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.
The PW.1 was cross
- examined at length by denying the negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

Thus, it can be concluded that, the negligence is on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.
12.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 insurance company that the FIR was registered against some unknown two wheeler and thereafter by colluding with the respondent No.1 the present vehicle falsely implicated by creating false story of accident.

Further,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 insurance company also gives stress on the point that the initial medical records discloses that the accident was between two motorcycles but later the fact was twisted by showing the petitioner as pedestrian.

Hence, prays to dismiss the petition on this two grounds by disputing involvement of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-54-R-0471.
13.
No doubt that, the Ex.P9 charge sheet was also came to be filed on the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA- 54-R-0471.

After detail investigation the I.O. has found that the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 was involved in the accident and accident was also caused by negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54- R-0471.
14.

In respect of defence taken by the respondent No.2 insurance company if we perused the medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P12 and very specifically if we see the OPD slip of ESI hospital dated 19.09.2023 it is mentioned as follows:
"Alleged history of RTA patient got hit from two wheeler while driving two wheeler at Channarayapatna on 18.09.2023."

The another OPD prescription dated 19.09.2023 of the ESI hospital is also available in Ex.P12 prescription wherein it is written as follows:
"Alleged history of RTA on 18.09.2023 at around 3.00 p.m., patient was sent causality".

4 15.

Thereby the two prescriptions of the same hospital even though states about the petitioner sustaining injury in the RTA, one prescription speaks about the petitioner was riding the two wheeler and another speaks about the petitioner sustained injuries in RTA.

On perusal of these two prescription it shows that in the prescription which is signed by Dr.Sudha shows that initially the said prescription was prepared by mentioning as only RTA and CMO was directed registered as MLC.
Thereafter the second detailed OPD slip was made wherein it says that the petitioner was riding the two wheeler and hit by another two wheeler.
The said two prescriptions of the same hospital shows the discrepancy in this regard.
Further on perusal of MLC register extract of Adichunchanagiri Hospital marked as Ex.P21 and 22 says that the petitioner sustained injury as he was pedestrian and hit by two wheeler.
As discussed above the accident spot was on the footpath.
In this case the eye witness is examined as PW.2.
The said PW.2 is the eye witness and numbered as witness number 3 in Ex.P9 charge sheet.
The said eye witness deposed that when the petitioner was walking on footpath the offending vehicle came and hit the petitioner on footpath.
The evidence of PW.2 eye witness supported with the Ex.P9 charge sheet.
The Ex.P9 charge sheet was filed by the investigating officer after detailed investigation.
The Investigating officer found after detailed investigation that the petitioner got hit by the two wheeler while he was walking on foot path.
Thereby, only minor discrepancies in the medical records the entire crime records cannot be discarded.
The FIR was registered within 2 days of the accident by saying as the petitioner was a pedestrian.
No grounds are made out to eschive the evidence of PW.2 eye witness.
16. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the negligent act by the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471.
17.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The charge sheet was came to be filed on the rider of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R- 0471 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC and Sec. 187 of IMV Act.

21. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 18.09.2023 which is caused by the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R-0471 which is belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
22.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-R- 0471.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 43 years.
As per the copy of Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P11 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 10.06.1980.
The accident was took place on 18.09.2023.
Thereby the age of the petitioner is considered as 43 years.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P15.

As per Ex.P15 the petitioner was admitted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre from 28.09.2023 to 11.10.2023 and has sustained comminuted fracture shaft of right tibia and underwent ORIF with IMIL.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.55,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P13 amounting to Rs.31,883/- and Ex.
P16 amounting to Rs.469/-
. The Ex.P13 and 16 bills are supported by medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P12 and Ex.P6 wound certificate and Ex.P15 discharge summary.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.32,400/-.

sentences.text: c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was doing agricultural work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But he has not produced any bank statement or pass book to show his income.
In the absence of evidence on income, the notional income of petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P15 - the petitioner was admitted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, from 28.09.2023 to 11.10.2023 totally for the period of 14 days.
Prior to that inpatient admission from the date of accident i.e., on 18.09.2023 to 28.09.2023 the petitioner took treatment in ESI hospital as per Ex.P12 for nearly 11 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 25 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months =
Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Sagar, Professor Orthopaedic AIMS Hospital, Bellur as PW.3.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner has sustained communited fracture of right tibia and underwent ORIF with IMIL.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.

Petitioner suffered disability of 26%
towards right lower limb.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
No other expert evidence is lead by the respondents to impeach the credibility of the evidence of PW.3 doctor.
In this case as per the evidence of PW.3 doctor who assessed the particular right lower limb disability of the petitioner at 26%.
As per the say of the petitioner he was doing coolie work and also agricultural work.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to greater extent.
The disability to the lower limb certainly effect any person particularly who is an agriculturist.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 18% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 14 X 18% = Rs.4,83,840/- which is the total loss of future income.
d) FOOD & NOURISHMENT;
As per Ex.P15 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 25 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P15 the injuries sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards food and nourishment.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P15 - the petitioner was admitted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, from 28.09.2023 to 11.10.2023 totally for the period of 14 days.

f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The petitioner got injuries in the alleged accident.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
h) Future Medical Expenses:- PW.3 doctor stated that the petitioner is suggested with implants removal and further assessment of knee for cruciate laxity.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.45,000/- under this head.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.7,70,240/-
